triggered_when_any: Project scope is new building
Project scope is new detached adu
Creates a new dwelling unit
Project scope is new attached adu
Addition area (sq ft) is more than 1000
Remodel, alteration or renovation (% of the building) is more than 50
all of: Landscape or hardscape work; and Fire Hazard Severity Zone is one of very_high
Fire Department site access plan required
not_triggered_when: The building is commercial, industrial or mixed use, or multifamily other than townhomes (the Fire Department review applies instead)
triggers.source: Matrix for Grading and Residential Fire Plan Review Determination, effective 08/13/2026

triggered_when_any: all of: Commercial, industrial or mixed-use building, or multifamily other than townhomes; and any of: Project scope is new building; or Addition area (sq ft) is more than 0; or Major remodel (as the City's Major Remodel handout decides it); or Change of occupancy group; or Tenant spaces joined, or a demising wall opened between them; or Work in an assembly space (A occupancy); or Commercial cooking equipment (range, oven, fryer, hood); or Battery energy storage system; or Fire sprinkler, fire alarm or fire monitoring work; or New or modified wireless facility; or Temporary tent, membrane structure or event booths; or Hazardous process or materials (spray booth, hazardous materials storage); or Fire Department site access plan required
staff_decide_when: Hotel or other lodging guest room or suite layout changes, with none of the triggers above

Part of the building's structure (roof, floor, exterior walls or overhangs) removed while the rest stays in use. Demolishing interior partitions or finishes inside a tenant improvement is not this case

The plans show removal or reinforcement of the building's structure (roof, floor, exterior walls or overhangs), or an addition, and the City's Major Remodel handout does not decide it or the numbers that would decide it are not on the plans
A grocery or food store adding refrigerated display or service-case equipment, with no cooking equipment
Work in a school, day care, care facility or other institutional occupancy (Group E, I or R-4), or in a high-rise, with none of the triggers above
The plans do not show the occupancy group or the suite boundaries, or the sheets that would show sprinkler or alarm scope are not in the set or contradict each other
not_triggered_when: The building is a single family home, duplex, ADU, JADU or townhome
Work on the City's over-the-counter list, a reroof, or a sign

Interior tenant improvement inside one office, retail, personal service or similar suite that stays in the same occupancy group, with no tenant spaces joined, no sprinkler or alarm work, no cooking equipment, no assembly room, no added floor area, and no removal or reinforcement of the building's structure (roof, floor, exterior walls or overhangs)
Exterior repair or refinish of an existing building with no added floor area (siding, stucco, awnings, stairs, windows or doors)
Interior repair (drywall, finishes, fixtures in place)
Interior remodel of a dwelling unit, a deck, or a balcony in a multifamily building with no change of occupancy and no added floor area
Demolition of an entire building, with no fire service or hydrant work
EV chargers, or solar with no battery storage
Removing a wireless facility with nothing added
Site work with no building (retaining wall, paving, parking, accessible route, playground)
triggers.source: LBFD "Construction & the Fire Code" page (multi-family, commercial and industrial new construction and remodel projects are routed to the Fire Department); Building Permit Issuance handout row 2 (Fire Department Approval criterion); CBC 1.11.1 and 1.11.2.1.1 (State Fire Marshal scope, enforced by the city fire department); LBMC 25.05.040(C)(4), 25.10.008(O) and 14.50.104 (CBC 903.6)
